_comment: REPORT LANGUAGE — everything the renderer prints that the ANALYST did not write. A report has two kinds of text and they must be treated differently. The FURNITURE (cover labels, running header, table-of-contents title, 'Appendix', figure and table captions, the audience stamp) is generated by the template, is finite, and can be swapped wholesale — that is what this file does. The BODY is the analyst's argument and is NEVER machine-translated by the tool: an assessment is written in one language from the start, because the estimative vocabulary ('we assess with high confidence') is a calibrated technical register and a paraphrase of it silently changes what the report claims. So `estimative_terms` is not a translation aid — it is the FIXED Vietnamese wording for each ICD-203 term, and an author writing a Vietnamese report uses these exact strings and no synonyms, exactly as an English report uses 'we assess' and not 'we think'. `section_names` does the same job for the house report structure, so a Vietnamese deliverable has the same skeleton as an English one and a reviewer can hold them side by side. Add a language by adding its key to every group. Nothing here is case data.

strings._comment: The generated furniture, per language code. Every key must exist in every language — a missing one falls back to English rather than printing an empty label, because a cover row with no label is a defect a reader notices. `basis_default` is the collection-basis line on the cover and is a CLAIM: leave it as passive only when the run really was passive (frontmatter `basis:` overrides it, and any run that fetched a live page, fingerprinted TLS or probed an endpoint must). `handling` prefixes the classification line; `appendix` becomes the section word once a report calls \appendix.

vi.audience_executive: Báo cáo tóm tắt cho lãnh đạo
vi.audience_le: Báo cáo phục vụ cơ quan chức năng

estimative_terms._comment: ICD-203 estimative language, and its FIXED Vietnamese wording. This is the one part of a report that must not be paraphrased: the terms are a calibrated scale, not stylistic choices, and 'có khả năng cao' and 'rất có thể' are not interchangeable once a reader is grading the judgement. An author writing in Vietnamese uses the string on the right verbatim, keeps the probability band, and — as in English — never mixes a confidence word ('we assess with HIGH CONFIDENCE', about the quality of the evidence) with a probability word ('LIKELY', about the event). `band` is the ICD-203 percentage range; quote it once in the report's methodology section so the reader can grade the scale rather than guess at it.

low_confidence.vi: chúng tôi đánh giá với độ tin cậy thấp

section_names._comment: The house report skeleton (IntelReport SKILL.md § 'Report structure'), named in each language. Use these headings verbatim so an English and a Vietnamese rendering of the same case have the same sections in the same order — a reviewer comparing them should be reading a translation, not a different report. The keys are the house section ids; the order here is the order in the document.
